meta.description: CPS bond series split into principal and interest (budget book Tables 2-3, official statements) with the revenue that pays each series

source.doc: CPS FY2026 Budget Book, Debt Management chapter, Tables 2 and 3
CPS FY2026 Budget Book, Debt Management chapter, Tables 2 and 3

side.label: Paid from: EBF. State aid (Evidence-Based Funding) is the first revenue pledged to this series.

source.doc: CPS FY2026 Budget Book, Debt Management chapter, Tables 2 and 3

side.note: Budget book p.220: CPS alternate revenue bonds are backed first by state aid, PPRT, City IGA revenue or federal subsidies, and second by a property tax levy that is abated (not collected) while the first source is available. Capital Improvement Tax bonds are paid only from the CIT levy.

pieces.name: Series 2009G: final repayment of the loan (principal)

source.doc: Official Statement, Series 2009G Qualified School Construction Bonds; CPS FY2026 Budget Book Table 2 note 2 and p.219 (sinking fund)

pieces.why: This is the last payment on a 2009 school-building loan. CPS saved this money in a sinking fund over 15 years, so it does not add to this year's operating cost.
pieces.note: Budget book: paid from a sinking fund funded by required deposits since FY2011 and 'did not add to the District's annual debt service costs funded by operations in FY2026'. Matures 12/15/2025.

pieces.name: Series 2009G: interest (1.75% supplemental coupon)

source.doc: Official Statement, Series 2009G Qualified School Construction Bonds; CPS FY2026 Budget Book Table 2 note 2 and p.219 (sinking fund)

pieces.note: $254,240,000 x 1.75% for one half year. Bonds were Qualified School Construction Bonds, so most of the investors' return was a federal tax credit.

splits.note: Principal is $254.2M of the $256.5M. The budget book says it is paid from a sinking fund saved up since FY2011, not from this year's revenue.

source.doc: CPS FY2026 Budget Book, Debt Management chapter, Tables 2 and 3
CPS FY2026 Budget Book, Debt Management chapter, Tables 2 and 3

side.label: Paid from: IGA / PPRT. Payments from the City of Chicago under an intergovernmental agreement (property taxes the City levies) and the State's Personal Property Replacement Tax are pledged to this series.

source.doc: CPS FY2026 Budget Book, Debt Management chapter, Tables 2 and 3

side.note: Budget book p.220: CPS alternate revenue bonds are backed first by state aid, PPRT, City IGA revenue or federal subsidies, and second by a property tax levy that is abated (not collected) while the first source is available. Capital Improvement Tax bonds are paid only from the CIT levy.

pieces.name: Series 1999A: principal repaid

source.doc: Official Statement, Unlimited Tax GO Bonds (Dedicated Tax Revenues) Series 1999A, inside cover and mandatory sinking fund schedule

pieces.why: This is the loan itself being paid back on 12/1/2025, split below into the two kinds of bond in this series.

children.name: Zero-coupon bonds (capital appreciation), original principal due 12/1/2025

source.doc: Official Statement, Unlimited Tax GO Bonds (Dedicated Tax Revenues) Series 1999A, inside cover and mandatory sinking fund schedule

children.why: The money borrowed in 1999 on bonds that pay nothing until they mature.
children.note: Official Statement: 2025 maturity original principal $8,215,896.00, $1,239.20 per $5,000 at maturity, so $33,150,000 at maturity.

children.name: Regular bonds called by the sinking fund schedule (term bonds due 2026)

source.doc: Official Statement, Unlimited Tax GO Bonds (Dedicated Tax Revenues) Series 1999A, inside cover and mandatory sinking fund schedule

children.why: A set yearly slice of the 5.5% term bonds that the 1999 documents require CPS to pay off each December 1.
children.note: Official Statement: mandatory sinking fund redemption of $27,165,000 on 12/1/2025.

pieces.name: Series 1999A: interest paid

source.doc: Official Statement, Unlimited Tax GO Bonds (Dedicated Tax Revenues) Series 1999A, inside cover and mandatory sinking fund schedule

pieces.why: This is the interest bill for the year, split below into built-up interest on the zero-coupon bonds and yearly interest on the regular bonds.

children.name: Built-up interest on the zero-coupon bonds (accreted interest)

source.doc: Official Statement, Unlimited Tax GO Bonds (Dedicated Tax Revenues) Series 1999A, inside cover and mandatory sinking fund schedule

children.why: Interest that piled up since 1999 on bonds that pay it all at the end.

children.name: Yearly interest on the 5.5% regular bonds

source.doc: Official Statement, Unlimited Tax GO Bonds (Dedicated Tax Revenues) Series 1999A, inside cover and mandatory sinking fund schedule

children.note: 5.5% x half year on $55,855,000 (Dec 2025) plus 5.5% x half year on $28,690,000 (Jun 2026), balances from the sinking fund schedule.

splits.note: Ties to the Official Statement: sinking fund $27,165,000 + zero-coupon maturity $33,150,000 + term-bond interest $2,324,987.50 = $62,639,987.50.

pieces.name: Series 1998B-1: money borrowed in 1998 (principal)

source.doc: Official Statement, Unlimited Tax GO Bonds (Dedicated Tax Revenues) Series 1998B-1, inside cover (2025 maturity)

pieces.why: In 1998 CPS borrowed this part. The bond pays nothing until the end, so this is the day the original loan is repaid.
pieces.note: Capital appreciation bond: it pays no interest each year. The Official Statement lists the 12/1/2025 maturity at $14,606,630.00 original principal and $59,000,000 total value at maturity ($1,237.85 per $5,000 at maturity).

pieces.name: Series 1998B-1: interest that built up since 1998 (accreted interest)

source.doc: Official Statement, Unlimited Tax GO Bonds (Dedicated Tax Revenues) Series 1998B-1, inside cover (2025 maturity)

pieces.why: This bond adds interest to what is owed for 27 years and pays it all on one day, so this is the interest bill that came due.
pieces.note: Equals $59,000,000 value at maturity minus $14,606,630 original principal.

splits.note: Whole FY2026 payment is the final value of the bonds that mature 12/1/2025 (capital appreciation bonds). It ties to the Official Statement: $59,000,000 at maturity.

side.note: Budget book p.220: CPS alternate revenue bonds are backed first by state aid, PPRT, City IGA revenue or federal subsidies, and second by a property tax levy that is abated (not collected) while the first source is available. Capital Improvement Tax bonds are paid only from the CIT levy.

splits.note: All interest this year, no principal is due until later (last payment 12/01/46). Paid from CIT.
